**Job Summary**

The Program Manager, Pre University Programs is responsible for the planning, development, delivery and evaluation of Extended Learning’s portfolio of educational programs for Canadian and international high school students. The portfolio includes UBC Future Global Leaders, a large summer program with academic, extracurricular and residential components, as well as year round online and applied technology programs. Serving more than 1,500 students annually and generating over $5 million in revenue.

The Manager leads program planning and manages the interdependent academic, staffing, financial and operational requirements of the portfolio. The role is accountable for program quality, student experience and welfare, and achievement of enrolment and financial targets. The Manager directs professional and support staff, supervises contract instructors, and oversees summer staff through the Student Life Manager, ensuring that teaching, activities and residence arrangements operate as a coordinated program.

The Manager develops program policies and delivery practices within ExL and UBC requirements, leads program improvement and new program development, and manages relationships that support recruitment and growth. The role is responsible for balancing educational objectives, financial sustainability and the needs of a diverse population of students aged 15 to 18, including international students requiring custodianship and residential support.  
  
**Organizational Status**

The position will report to the Director, Strategic Partnerships and Programs. The Manager works with instructors, faculty, program staff, the ExL marketing team, International Student Initiative and Student Recruitment to plan and deliver the portfolio. The role maintains relationships with external educational partners and recruitment stakeholders and serves as a point of contact for parents on matters affecting their children’s participation and welfare.  
  
**Work Performed**  
  
**Program Planning and Development**

* Leads the development of goals, priorities and plans for ExL’s pre university portfolio, translating program objectives into educational offerings and delivery requirements.
* Conducts market research, assesses student needs, and exchanges information with other universities offering pre university programs to identify opportunities for new offerings, improvement and growth.
* Manages the development and delivery of summer, online and applied technology programs, including the review and redesign of existing offerings, considering educational value, student needs, delivery capacity and financial sustainability.
* Oversees the development and delivery of non credit academic courses taught at the first year university level, working with instructors to ensure that content and teaching approaches are appropriately adapted for domestic and international high school students.
* Oversees university preparation workshops and lectures delivered by ExL instructors and contractors, ensuring that offerings support program objectives and students’ transition to university learning.
* Leads program evaluation and uses findings to improve curriculum, teaching practices, delivery arrangements and student experience.

**Student Experience and Welfare**

* Oversees the planning and delivery of on campus and off campus extracurricular activities for the Future Global Leaders summer program at UBC Vancouver.
* Manages the residential component through the Student Life Manager and summer staff team, ensuring that students are appropriately supervised and that residence arrangements support their safety and participation in the program.
* Manages complex student welfare and conduct matters, including injuries requiring hospitalization, homesickness and mental health concerns, and coordinates appropriate responses with staff and relevant services.
* Serves as a point of contact for parents regarding student concerns and incidents and acts as the designated custodian for international students as required.
* Leads the development and delivery of bursaries and other financial benefits.

* Develops the annual budget for the pre university portfolio, accounting for academic delivery, staffing, residence, activities, marketing and other operating requirements.
* Sets and manages gross and net revenue targets and is responsible for achieving the portfolio’s budget objectives.
* Oversees and approves expenditures within the annual budget, including payroll for program staff. Monitors financial performance and manages resources in relation to enrolment, delivery requirements and program commitments.
* Provides program marketing direction and budget to the ExL marketing team, working with the team to develop and implement marketing strategies and approving program marketing materials.
* Provides direction and budget for International Student Initiative and Student Recruitment activities promoting Future Global Leaders.
* Leads social media activities for the pre university portfolio, ensuring that promotional content reflects program offerings and intended audiences.
* Develops business opportunities and maintains partnerships with external stakeholders, including BC Offshore Schools, to promote programs, support student recruitment and contribute to portfolio growth and sustainability.
* Participates in relevant professional associations, including the Association for Pre College Program Directors, to maintain professional networks and inform program practices.

* Develops and implements student and program policies and procedures, including those addressing student conduct, registration, withdrawals and refunds, within ExL and UBC requirements.
* Oversees improvements to administrative processes and the use of technology to support educational delivery and improve coordination, consistency and efficiency across the portfolio.

**Résumé**
L’initiative AI Fabric de Bell est à l’avant-garde de la création d’un réseau canadien de calcul d’intelligence artificielle sécurisé et souverain. À titre de directeur(trice) de programme, vous serez responsable de la réalisation de bout en bout du programme national de construction des centres de données. Vous assurerez la coordination de la portée, des échéanciers, des budgets et de l’exécution interfonctionnelle à travers plusieurs sites réalisés simultanément. Vous agirez comme force d’intégration entre les équipes de construction, d’ingénierie, de mise en service, d’approvisionnement et de contrôle de programme afin de garantir une livraison prévisible et bien gouvernée. **Principales responsabilités**

* Assumer l’entière responsabilité de la livraison du programme national de construction des centres de données, en assurant l’intégration de la portée, des échéanciers, des budgets et des exigences de qualité à travers plusieurs sites réalisés en parallèle.
* Orchestrer l’exécution interfonctionnelle entre les équipes de construction, d’ingénierie, de mise en service, d’approvisionnement et de contrôle de programme afin d’assurer l’alignement sur les objectifs du programme.
* Établir et gouverner le cadre de réalisation du programme, incluant les points de contrôle décisionnels (stage gates), les jalons, les mécanismes de gouvernance et les responsabilités décisionnelles à l’échelle du portefeuille.
* Assurer la responsabilité du calendrier directeur intégré ainsi que du budget global du programme, en favorisant la prévisibilité, la transparence et la rigueur dans la gestion des échéanciers pour l’ensemble des projets.
* Diriger la gestion des risques, la gouvernance des changements et la gestion des interdépendances à l’échelle du programme, en identifiant et en résolvant les enjeux systémiques avant qu’ils n’affectent la livraison.
* Fournir des rapports de niveau exécutif à la direction du Réseau d'IA tissé de Bell et des Programmes d’investissement, en transformant des informations complexes sur l’avancement des projets en analyses claires facilitant la prise de décision.
* Superviser les aspects financiers du programme, les prévisions budgétaires et la planification des investissements en partenariat avec les équipes des finances et du contrôle de programme.
* Diriger la planification et la priorisation des ressources à travers les différents sites afin d’équilibrer les besoins concurrents à mesure que le programme prend de l’expansion.
* Développer et faire évoluer les capacités de gestion de programme de Bell à une étape clé de croissance, en implantant des processus reproductibles, des guides d’exécution et des mécanismes de transfert des leçons apprises à travers le portefeuille.
* Agir à titre de principal point d’escalade et d’interlocuteur exécutif auprès des directeurs de site, des responsables fonctionnels et des partenaires externes chargés de la livraison.

**Qualifications Essentielles**

* Plus de 15 années d’expérience dans la direction de grands programmes d’investissement, incluant une expérience directe dans des centres de données hyperscale ou des infrastructures critiques (portefeuilles multisites et de plusieurs milliards de dollars privilégiés).
* Feuille de route démontrée dans la gestion complète de programmes comportant plusieurs projets de construction exécutés simultanément, et non uniquement dans la gestion de projets individuels.
* Excellente maîtrise des disciplines de gestion de programme, notamment la planification intégrée, le contrôle des coûts et des budgets, la gestion des risques et la gouvernance des changements.
* Solide compréhension de l’ensemble du cycle de livraison d’un centre de données, incluant la construction, l’ingénierie, les systèmes MEP et la mise en service jusqu’au transfert aux opérations.
* Capacité démontrée à intégrer, coordonner et mobiliser des équipes interfonctionnelles diversifiées ainsi que des partenaires externes de réalisation.
* Expertise reconnue en gouvernance de programme, en gestion par étapes décisionnelles (stage-gate) et en présentation de rapports à la haute direction.
* Forte présence exécutive et excellentes compétences relationnelles permettant d’influencer et de remettre en question de façon constructive des leaders de l’ingénierie, de la construction, des finances et de la haute direction.
* Expérience dans la création et le développement d’une organisation de gestion de programme à partir d’une phase de démarrage ou de mise en place.
* Diplôme universitaire en génie, en gestion de la construction ou dans une discipline connexe; les titres professionnels PMP, PgMP, ing. ou une certification équivalente sont fortement privilégiés.
* Disponibilité à voyager à l’échelle nationale entre les différents sites de construction à mesure que le portefeuille de projets prend de l’expansion.

**About the Role**
Cogeco is looking for a hands-on, impact-driven Product Owner to drive practical AI adoption across our functional departments. Operating at the intersection of program leadership, process redesign, and change enablement, you will help our internal teams re-engineer their daily workflows to become truly AI-native.
  
  
Working closely with functional business leaders, our AI Center of Excellence, and IT/Security teams, you will own the end-to-end roadmap for functional AI enablement, identify high-value AI use cases, and build scalable upskilling programs that turn everyday employees into confident AI practitioners.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own the Functional AI Program Roadmap: Define the multi-quarter program vision, quarterly objectives, and delivery priorities for departmental AI adoption, balancing immediate team wins with long-term scalability.
* Redesign Workflows & Curate AI Use Cases: Partner with functional departments to spot bottlenecks, re-imagine processes with AI, and manage a prioritized backlog of reusable AI patterns—routing them to self-serve tools, custom platform builds, or employee training modules.
* Drive Solution Delivery & Backlog Execution: Translate high-value AI use cases into clear requirements and MVP scopes, working alongside engineering and platform partners to deliver practical workflow solutions on schedule.
* Scale the AI Power User Program: Design and run repeatable cohort-based training programs—complete with selection criteria, curriculum, certification, and communities of practice—to build grassroots AI fluency across the company.
* Measure & Communicate Business Impact: Establish a clear value-tracking framework (measuring time saved, cost reduction, quality gains, and adoption rates) to prove ROI and guide ongoing investment decisions.
* Manage AI License Access, Budgets & Governance: Assess departmental tool needs and own the end-to-end access process—including intake requests, license and quota allocation, budget tracking, and coordinating security and privacy reviews.
* Lead Change Management & Adoption: Partner with department leaders to build tailored adoption roadmaps, overcome resistance to new workflows, and embed AI habits into daily operations across non-technical teams.

**What You Bring**

* Program & Transformation Leadership: 7+ years of experience leading complex programs, digital transformation initiatives, or business process redesign, with a strong track record of taking projects from concept to sustained adoption.
* Outcome-Focused Pattern Recognition: Ability to cut through AI hype to focus on measurable time savings and quality gains, while spotting repeatable patterns across departments to scale one team's clever workaround into an enterprise-wide solution.
* Change Management & Enablement: Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change—building adoption strategies, running workshops, and coaching non-technical stakeholders to embrace new ways of working.
* Hands-On Applied AI Fluency: Practical, working experience with modern generative AI tools (e.g., Gemini, Claude, Copilot) and a solid grasp of prompt engineering, automation, and agentic workflows.
* Agile Execution: Proven experience managing prioritized backlogs, defining MVPs, writing clear user stories, and driving iterative delivery within cross-functional agile teams.
* Builder & Coach Mindset: Just as comfortable scoping a workflow requirement or testing a new AI tool yourself as you are guiding a non-technical team through their first automation.
* Operational & Governance Acumen: Experience managing software license access and budgets, alongside familiarity with enterprise data privacy, security, and governance standards (considered an asset).
* Fluency in English and French (spoken and written) required to collaborate with stakeholders in Quebec, Ontario, and across the United States.
* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field

Ikotek | Product Development | ODM Projects | Vancouver R&D Center

**About the Role**

As PDM for North America, you own ODM projects from RFQ through mass production. You will drive profitability, technical execution, and customer growth, bridging engineering, supply chain, and sales.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Project P&L and Ownership**

* Own the profit and loss (P&L) of ODM projects. Ensure milestones, delivery schedules, and financial targets are met.
* Steer the development lifecycle from specification through delivery.

**Account Management and Growth**

* Maintain existing client relationships and proactively identify new customer accounts and RFQ opportunities in the North American market.

**RFQ, Quotation, and Commercial Strategy**

* Lead RFQ presentations of company capabilities. Analyze customer requirements and coordinate internal technical proposals covering industrial design (ID), mechanical design (MD), hardware (HW), and BOM.
* Consolidate internal cost estimates, including BOM, R&D and production NRE, tooling, and certifications. Partner with Sales to review and release competitive quotations.

**Project Governance**

* Draft Statements of Work (SOW). Run internal and external project kick-offs and define product specifications.

**Supply Chain and Operations Oversight**

* Oversee key supplier sourcing and review EMS factory quotations. Analyze MOQ and lead times.
* Monitor sample validation through to mass-production delivery.

**Requirements**

* 5+ years of experience in product development, technical program management, or engineering management within an ODM, OEM, or EMS ecosystem.
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (mechanical, electrical, or a related technical field), or in Business Administration with a strong technical background.
* Deep industry knowledge of IoT ecosystems for the North American market, including smart home automation, telematics and fleet management, and AI cameras.
* Demonstrated experience managing project P&L, commercial agreements, and complex Statements of Work (SOW).
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with a track record of leading technical RFQ workshops and steering senior-level customer relationships.
* Strong understanding of hardware product lifecycles, including ID, MD, hardware architecture, and BOM cost structures.
* Familiarity with cellular (5G, 4G/LTE, RedCap), short-range wireless (BLE, Wi-Fi, Thread/Zigbee), or specialized communication protocols.
* Experience working with electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and component suppliers, negotiating pricing, and managing NRE and tooling allocations.

**About Ikotek**

Ikotek is a global IoT original design manufacturer (ODM), headquartered in San Diego, California. We serve OEM customers worldwide with end-to-end services, from design through manufacturing and certification.

We focus on enterprise cellular (NB-IoT, 5G), satellite, and AIoT solutions. In January 2026 we expanded manufacturing to Mexico, adding capacity and TAA-compliant supply.

Website: www.ikotek.com

**Industries & Applications**

Ikotek's ODM services power connected products across a range of industries, including:

* **Asset Tracking and Logistics:**
  tracking devices and connected asset solutions.
* **Fleet and Connected Vehicles:**
  dash cams and telematics hardware.
* **Smart Metering and Smart Grid:**
  metering and grid hardware.
* **Point of Sale and Handhelds:**
  POS terminals and handheld devices.
* **Satellite and AIoT:**
  connected devices using satellite links and AI-enabled IoT.

**Why Ikotek?**

* **Global Impact, Local Presence:**
  Work on connected products for OEM customers worldwide, from a North American team.
* **Enterprise IoT Focus:**
  Own projects from first RFQ through certification and mass production.
* **Career Growth:**
  Join a growing, dedicated IoT business with a clear path to bigger, more challenging projects.
* **Global Team:**
  Collaborate with engineering, supply chain, and commercial teams across regions.

**Our Culture**

We bring a global mindset to every project and turn complex hardware into reliable, production-ready products.

We work as one global team, collaborating closely across R&D, supply chain, and customer teams.

We value technical sharing and mentorship. Senior team members help grow the people around them.

We take wellbeing seriously, with flexible working arrangements and support for work-life balance.

We grow together, with real advancement opportunities and a clear path to bigger projects.

**What Life Looks Like**

* Hybrid work from the Vancouver R&D Center, with flexible start times and work-from-home days for early or late global meetings.
* Your week mixes supplier and factory calls, RFQ and design reviews, and customer updates.
* Some meetings run early or late to cover global time zones.
* You will see the products you shape reach customers.
* Regular team events, including holiday parties, summer retreats, and celebrations throughout the year.

**Company-Paid Benefits**

* 100% company-paid health, dental ($2,000/year), vision ($450 every two years, including $100 for an eye exam), and unlimited prescription drugs. Coverage is active from day one with no waiting period.
* $500/year each for massage, chiropractic, psychologist, acupuncture, and physiotherapy.

**Primary Responsibilities**

* Guide new customers through the onboarding process to ensure a successful implementation

**What great looks like at Magma**

* Skills, Knowledge & Problem Solving: you build trusted partnerships with several stakeholders per customer, frame every conversation around impact and success criteria, and act as a trusted pedagogical advisor.

* Diplomacy, tact, and poise under pressure when working through customer issues.
* Bachelor’s degree from a 4-year institution.

**An ideal candidate also has:**

* Strong bias for action, the ability to think big, with insistence on high standards.
* Experience serving and supporting large-scale business solutions at Fortune 500 companies.
* Thrives in an unstructured, fast-paced, and change-heavy environment.
* French Fluency is a plus.

**POSITION SUMMARY**  
The Operations Manager is responsible for the safe, efficient, and coordinated operation of the entire facility. The role provides leadership and oversight across all departments, personnel, production activities, material movement, equipment, maintenance coordination, inventory, shipping, and site support functions. The Operations Manager ensures departments work together to achieve safety, production, quality, customer service, budget, and cost objectives through effective planning, resource use, and cost-conscious decision-making.

**Reports To:** Site Manager

**Primary Scope:** All facility departments and operations

**CORE RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Safety and Compliance**

* Lead a strong safety culture and ensure safe work practices are consistently followed throughout the facility.
* Ensure compliance with company policies, procedures, permits, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Ensure workplace inspections, safety observations, incident investigations, and corrective actions are completed.
* Confirm employees are trained, competent, and properly equipped to perform assigned work safely.
* Partner with site safety resources to address hazards, manage change, and improve safety performance.

  

**Facility Operations**

* Oversee day-to-day operations across all departments and work areas within the facility.
* Coordinate production, yard, shipping, receiving, inventory, maintenance, and support activities to maintain safe and efficient workflow.
* Provide direct oversight of whole-tire receiving, shred product shipments, tire wire loading, GMT tire receiving and shearing, and OTR tire receiving and shearing.
* Monitor operational performance and adjust labour, equipment, and priorities to meet production and customer requirements.
* Ensure site organization, housekeeping, material storage, traffic flow, and inventory controls are maintained.

  

**Leadership and People Management**

* Provide leadership and direction to department supervisors, leads, and employees.
* Establish daily priorities, assign resources, and ensure clear accountability for results.
* Support employee onboarding, training, development, coaching, and performance management.
* Promote teamwork, respectful communication, and effective coordination between departments.
* Address operational concerns promptly and escalate significant risks or business impacts as required.

  

**Planning and Coordination**

* Develop and communicate daily and weekly operating plans based on production schedules, inbound volume, shipping demand, staffing, and equipment availability.
* Coordinate department activities to prevent bottlenecks, delays, product contamination, or excess inventory.
* Work with Transportation, Maintenance, Sales, Customer Service, and other support functions to meet site and customer needs.
* Plan for weather, seasonal volume changes, shutdowns, contractor work, and other conditions that may affect operations.
* Participate in budgeting, forecasting, and monthly cost review activities by providing operational input, identifying cost pressures, and supporting corrective actions when spending or performance varies from plan.
* Evaluate labour, equipment, contractor, material handling, and operating decisions with consideration for cost, service impact, safety, and long-term site performance.

  

**Equipment and Maintenance**

* Ensure pre-use inspections and required equipment checks are completed and documented.
* Coordinate preventive maintenance, repairs, breakdown response, and equipment availability with Maintenance.
* Ensure equipment is operated safely, within capacity, and only by trained and authorized employees.
* Support equipment replacement, site improvement, and capital planning by identifying operational needs and risks.

  

**Performance and Continuous Improvement**

* Monitor safety, production, quality, downtime, inventory, labour, budget, and cost performance, including trends that affect operating efficiency or financial results.
* Identify and implement practical improvements that reduce risk, waste, delays, rework, and operating cost.
* Support cost-benefit evaluation of operational improvements, equipment needs, staffing changes, and process changes before implementation.
* Use operational data, employee input, inspections, and incident findings to improve processes and controls.
* Complete required operational reports and communicate significant issues, trends, and actions to site leadership.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience leading operations in an industrial, manufacturing, recycling, logistics, or similar environment.
* Proven experience supervising multiple work groups, departments, or operational functions.
* Strong safety leadership, planning, decision-making, organizational, and communication skills.
* Working knowledge of material handling, mobile equipment, production processes, inventory control, and maintenance coordination.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and respond effectively to changing operating conditions.
* Ability to understand budgets, track operating costs, review performance against plan, and support financial decision-making in an operations environment.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and operational reporting systems.

  

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

* Industrial environment with regular work in both indoor and outdoor operating areas.
* Exposure to weather, dust, noise, mobile equipment, and active production processes.
* Frequent walking and site presence are required to oversee operations and support employees.
* Overtime, weekend work, and after-hours response may be required based on operational needs.

At Ntiva, we’re more than a Managed Services Provider, we’re a community dedicated to helping each other, our clients, and their businesses thrive both personally and professionally. Ntiva is a culture of people who are passionate about the work…and each other.
  
  
Our clients view us as an essential part of their teams, relying on us for strategic guidance, fast solutions to complex challenges, and proactive support. With strategic locations across the U.S. and leadership from our founder, Steven Freidkin, we’re on the front lines of a fast-paced industry, facing cybersecurity threats and rapid technology changes together.
  
  
If you thrive in a dynamic, supportive environment and enjoy going above and beyond, we’d love to meet you. Come explore one of our many opportunities and grow with us!
  
  
**How You'll Make An Impact**
As Manager, Service Delivery – Field Operations, you'll lead the dedicated team of field technicians who handle every onsite visit, installation and project engagement in Ntiva's Chicago and Indiana markets. When a client needs someone in the room, your team is who shows up: prepared, on time and able to finish the job.
  
  
You'll run field operations like a business. That means scheduling and dispatching against real demand, keeping utilization healthy, making sure onsite work is scoped correctly before it's sold, and turning schedule gaps into ticket capacity that helps the Service Desk pods. Just as importantly, you'll coach and develop your technicians, helping them grow while raising the bar for every onsite experience.
  
  
Success in this role isn't just about getting techs out the door. It's about building a field team clients trust, using every hour well, and delivering results you can see and measure.
  
  
**Location and work expectations**

* Hybrid with 20% being onsite/80% being remote, based out of Ntiva's Chicago headquarters, with regular travel to client sites across the Chicago and Indiana markets as field work, escalations and client meetings require.
* A valid driver's license and reliable transportation are required.
* Core schedule Monday–Friday, 8:00am–5:00pm local, with some after-hours and weekend work for maintenance windows and cutovers.
* You participate in the Service Delivery management escalation rotation.
* This role involves driving between sites, extended periods of standing or sitting, lifting and carrying IT equipment (up to 50 lbs), and working in server rooms, comms closets and other client spaces.

**What You Will Be Doing**
Own onsite delivery
  
  

* Own outcomes for all onsite work in the Chicago and Indiana markets: break/fix dispatches, installs, moves/adds/changes and project field work.
* Serve as the escalation point for onsite issues, and own client-impacting onsite incidents end to end, including the client conversation, root cause and corrective action through to closure.
* Make sure every technician works safely and follows each client's site rules, access procedures and security requirements while onsite.
* Partner with Account Managers and Solution Architects so field work is scoped accurately (hours, skills, materials and site requirements) before it is sold.
* Help integrate the field staff and clients of newly acquired companies into the Ntiva regional model.
* Manage the third-party vendors involved in onsite work, such as cabling contractors, internet providers and hardware vendors, holding them to the same service standards as your own team.

Schedule and dispatch the field team
  
  

* Work with the Dispatch Coordinators to schedule and route all onsite work, balancing planned projects against reactive dispatches and assigning each visit to the nearest technician with the right skills to keep drive time and repeat trips to a minimum.
* Make sure every technician arrives prepared, with ticket history, site documentation and access confirmed, and hardware and parts coordinated with procurement from order to onsite installation.
* Plan coverage for maintenance windows, weekend cutovers and time off, so no client site depends on a single person.
* Make sure onsite changes follow Ntiva's change management process, so installs, cutovers and maintenance work are planned, approved and communicated.

Put downtime to work
  
  

* When the field schedule has gaps, direct technicians to remote tickets, partnering with the Service Desk pod managers on where help is needed most.
* Agree clear handoffs with the pods, so tickets move to the field only when an onsite visit is truly needed and return cleanly once the visit is complete.

Lead and grow the team
  
  

* Coach each technician through a personal growth plan using Ntiva's structured development framework, and champion their promotion when they're ready. Set yearly team goals and run annual assessments.
* Run the team's weekly Level 10 meeting and hold weekly one-on-ones with each direct report covering feedback, growth and performance.
* Hire field talent: review resumes, interview and evaluate candidates.
* Make sure every direct report has the training and certifications their work requires.
* Set clear expectations and hold people accountable, coaching first and taking formal action, up to and including termination, when required.
* Handle admin for your direct reports: approve time off, review timesheets and approve expense reports.

Manage capacity like a business
  
  

* Understand field demand (dispatch volume, project hours, drive time and effort per visit) and plan capacity against it.
* Manage utilization to a healthy, sustainable band and flag capacity risk early, with numbers.
* Make the case for new or backfilled roles with data, weighing process change, routing and reallocation alongside hiring.

Deliver to the numbers
  
  

* Be directly accountable for the Field Operations scorecard (see What success looks like below), including project hours delivered against scope.
* Identify recurring onsite issues and drive permanent fixes rather than repeat visits.
* Ensure ticket data is complete and accurate, including time and travel entries and notes completed before leaving site, so the team's work is visible and measurable.

Raise the bar
  
  

* Reinforce Ntiva's values through daily actions and expectations.
* Contribute ideas for innovation and best practice across service delivery leadership, including automation and AI-assisted scheduling and dispatch.
* Invest in your own growth and take part in company-wide initiatives.

You'll be successful in this role if you bring
  
  

* 5+ years in IT, including at least 3 in a Managed Services Provider or comparable multi-client environment, with hands-on field or onsite experience.
* 2+ years of direct people management, including hiring, performance management and development. Required for external candidates; internal candidates may substitute demonstrated team lead or escalation lead experience.
* Experience scheduling and dispatching field technicians across multiple client sites.
* Hands-on infrastructure grounding in networking, firewalls, servers and end-user hardware: enough to judge the work, coach it and sanity-check an onsite escalation. Leadership, judgment and communication weigh more heavily than the depth of technical expertise.
* Working fluency with service delivery data. You can read a ticket or utilization report, question it and build an argument from it. Comfort with ConnectWise Manage reporting and BI dashboards is expected.
* Comfort delivering candid feedback and holding difficult conversations, with clients as well as with staff.
* The ability to communicate professionally in English, in writing and in person, to explain technical issues to non-technical people, and to present to managers and clients.
* ITIL 4 Foundation, or willingness to obtain it within the first six months.

* Experience with fund administration platforms, transfer agency systems, reporting tools, and Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, and Outlook.
* Ability to quickly learn and adapt to new systems, processes, and business requirements.

The VP, Operations & Patient Experience leads the teams that deliver care and support to every LifeMD patient. The role oversees about 150 people across clinical support operations (medical assistants, scheduling and clinical program management), the patient care center (customer service, care navigation, sales and quality assurance), and the operations function that keeps the business running (program management, procurement and inventory).

The VP serves as the central hub connecting every part of the business to the patient. Delivering high-quality care depends on ongoing collaboration with marketing, technology, finance, pharmacy and LifeMD's affiliated medical group: aligning patient support capacity with marketing's acquisition and retention plans, shaping the product and technology roadmap around what patients and care teams need, partnering with finance on budgets, KPIs and unit economics, and working with pharmacy and providers so every patient's care, from visit to medication, is seamless.

The Director of Quality is responsible for leading the organization's Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI), risk management, patient safety, accreditation, regulatory compliance, and performance improvement programs. This position provides strategic and operational leadership to ensure the delivery of safe, high-quality, patient-centered care while maintaining compliance with federal, state, and accreditation standards.

The Director collaborates with medical staff, nursing leadership, department directors, and executive leadership to develop a culture of continuous improvement, regulatory readiness, patient safety, and organizational excellence. **Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

**Quality and Performance Improvement**

* Lead and oversee the hospital's Quality Assessment and Performance Improvement (QAPI) Program.
* Collect, analyze, interpret, and report quality, patient safety, and performance improvement data.
* Develop, implement, and monitor quality indicators, dashboards, scorecards, and performance metrics.
* Facilitate performance improvement projects utilizing evidence-based methodologies and best practices.
* Coordinate organization-wide quality improvement initiatives to improve clinical outcomes, patient experience, and operational effectiveness.
* Prepare and present quality reports to leadership, medical staff committees, quality committees, and the Governing Board.
* Conduct audits, chart reviews, tracers, and compliance assessments to identify opportunities for improvement.

**Risk Management and Patient Safety**

* Direct the organization's risk management and patient safety programs.
* Investigate adverse events, patient complaints, grievances, safety events, near misses, and claims.
* Perform root cause analyses (RCA), failure mode and effects analyses (FMEA), and corrective action planning.
* Identify organizational risks and implement strategies to reduce patient, staff, and visitor harm.
* Monitor trends and implement proactive risk reduction initiatives.
* Collaborate with leadership to develop and monitor corrective action plans and ensure sustained improvements.

**Regulatory Compliance and Accreditation**

* Ensure compliance with CMS Conditions of Participation, Critical Access Hospital regulations, Texas Department of State Health Services requirements, and other applicable federal and state regulations.
* Coordinate survey readiness activities and accreditation preparation.
* Develop, review, implement, and maintain policies, procedures, and compliance programs.
* Coordinate responses to regulatory agencies and external surveyors.
* Monitor regulatory changes and communicate requirements throughout the organization.

**Utilization Review and Resource Management**

* Coordinate activities associated with utilization review and clinical resource management.
* Monitor appropriate utilization of healthcare resources and patient care services.
* Evaluate admission, continued stay, and discharge practices for regulatory and quality compliance.
* Analyze utilization data and recommend improvements in resource management and care coordination.
* Collaborate with managed care organizations, payers, and review organizations as appropriate.

**Leadership and Staff Development**

* Supervise and mentor quality analytics personnel.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous learning.
* Provide education and consultation to leaders, providers, and staff regarding quality, patient safety, and regulatory compliance.

The Director, IT Infrastructure and Operations leads the teams that keep Liquidity Services’ technology operating reliably every day: Platform Operations, Network Engineering, and Service Desk and Field Support. This role is accountable for the reliability, security, scalability, and cost-effectiveness of end-user support; server, identity, collaboration, backup, and storage platforms across on-premises, Azure, and AWS environments; and the hybrid network that connects offices, retail locations, warehouse facilities, cloud environments, and remote users. As a hands-on technical leader, the Director sets operational standards and service levels, serves as the senior escalation point for infrastructure and network issues, builds and develops the team, manages vendors and budgets, and leads modernization efforts in partnership with Information Security, DevOps, application teams, and business leaders. Based in the Dallas area, the Director works on-site at the Richardson, TX office several days a week and serves as the senior IT operations leader for that location.
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Service availability: Uptime of critical infrastructure, network, and end-user services meets defined targets.
* Service Desk performance: Response time, resolution time, first-contact resolution, backlog, and employee satisfaction meet agreed service levels.
* Security and compliance: Servers, endpoints, and network devices are kept current on security patches, vulnerabilities are remediated on schedule, and infrastructure controls pass PCI and SOX audits.
* Resilience: Backups and disaster recovery are tested regularly and meet defined recovery goals.
* Modernization delivery: The infrastructure and network roadmap is executed on schedule and within budget, including removing the dependency on Cisco cloud services routers and delivering new facility builds and site upgrades.
* Financial management: Infrastructure, cloud, telecom, and support spending is managed within budget, with measurable licensing, cloud, and vendor cost savings.
* Team strength: Strong retention, development, and coverage of critical skills across all three teams.
* Lead, manage, and develop the Platform Operations, Network Engineering, and Service Desk and Field Support teams, including hiring, goal setting, performance management, coaching, and succession planning.
* Set the strategy and multi-year roadmap for end-user support, infrastructure, and network services, aligned with business priorities, security requirements, and the company’s cloud direction.

Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance team helps the company meet its legal and regulatory obligations as our products, customers, and global footprint grow. We're looking for a Manager, Compliance & Regulatory Operations to lead the team that handles regulatory requests and complaints, copyright notices, and sanctions screening and operations.

The NOC Supervisor is the essential, shift-level manager responsible for the stable, efficient, and reliable day-to-day operation of the network infrastructure. This supervisor ensures staff adherence to all procedures, manages workload prioritization, and serves as the primary escalation point for frontline NOC Analysts and Technicians, driving incident response to meet critical Service Level Agreements (SLAs) during their shift.

**Daily Operations & Workload Management :**

* Shift Command: Oversee all day-to-day NOC activities during the assigned shift.
* Workload Distribution: Review and assign all incoming work, including automated alerts, trouble tickets, service requests, and change orders, ensuring proper prioritization and timely resolution by NOC staff.
* Performance Monitoring: Ensure the team is diligently monitoring all network and system health dashboards, performance metrics, and alerts using monitoring tools.
* SLA Compliance: Drive the team to meet or exceed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for response time (MTTA) and resolution time (MTTR).

* Communication Hub: Ensure clear, timely, and effective internal and external communication regarding the status of all significant incidents and maintenance activities.
* Problem Prevention: Lead preliminary root cause analysis (RCA) on recurring incidents and collaborate with the Problem Management team to find and eliminate systemic issues.

This position is responsible for coordinating the identification, investigation, escalation, resolution, and mitigation of complex network and cybersecurity incidents while minimizing operational disruptions and maintaining the availability, integrity, and security of enterprise infrastructure.

The Senior Network Incident Manager will serve as a trusted advisor to customer stakeholders, coordinating with network engineering, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and operations teams to resolve mission-critical incidents, improve incident management processes, and strengthen enterprise network resilience.

* Network Incident Management and Resolution: Lead the end-to-end lifecycle of network incidents, including identification, classification, prioritization, investigation, escalation, containment, remediation, service restoration, and closure across enterprise network environments.
* Technical Leadership and Troubleshooting: Provide senior-level technical guidance in diagnosing and resolving complex network outages, performance degradation, connectivity issues, configuration errors, and cybersecurity-related network incidents.
* Incident Response Coordination: Coordinate incident response activities across Network Operations Centers (NOCs), Security Operations Centers (SOCs), network engineering teams, cybersecurity personnel, infrastructure teams, and third-party service providers to ensure timely incident resolution.
* Root Cause Analysis and Continuous Improvement: Lead root cause analysis, problem management activities, and post-incident reviews to identify underlying technical deficiencies, develop corrective actions, and prevent recurring network incidents.
* Incident Governance and Performance Management: Establish and maintain incident management procedures, escalation protocols, operational playbooks, service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs), and reporting mechanisms to improve incident response effectiveness.
* Network Security and Architecture Advisory: Provide subject matter expertise supporting secure network architectures, enterprise cybersecurity strategies, network resilience, risk management, regulatory compliance, and the implementation of mission-critical network capabilities.
* Stakeholder Management and Executive Reporting: Serve as a primary point of coordination during major network incidents, providing timely status updates, impact assessments, executive briefings, after-action reports, and actionable recommendations to customer stakeholders while mentoring technical personnel.

### **Position Requirements**

* Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Network Engineering, or a related field.
* Minimum of five (5) years of professional experience in network engineering, network operations, cybersecurity operations, IT incident management, or related enterprise technology disciplines, with demonstrated experience managing complex network incidents.
* Demonstrated experience managing the incident management lifecycle, including incident prioritization, escalation, technical coordination, service restoration, root cause analysis, and post-incident reporting.
* Strong technical knowledge of enterprise networking technologies, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, routing and switching, BGP, OSPF, VLANs, VPNs, firewalls, load balancers, and network segmentation.

**Job Summary**

The Frontline Services Technician I is a technical role responsible for providing professional end-user support, monitoring IT infrastructure, resolving routine incidents, and escalating complex or high-risk issues.

This is a combined Service Desk, Network Operations, and Security Operations position. Technicians are expected to maintain broad foundational competency across all three areas while developing a primary focus in either End User Support or Network & Security Operations.

The role operates primarily through established procedures, knowledge articles, runbooks, and escalation processes.

This is an in-office position.

**Essential Functions**

* Provide technical support for end users, applications, endpoints, network connectivity, and common IT services, resolving routine issues using established troubleshooting procedures, knowledge articles, and runbooks.
* Provide responsive user support by answering service desk queue calls, responding to email and portal-generated tickets, and communicating clearly and professionally with users by phone and email throughout the lifecycle of incidents and service requests.
* Monitor and respond to service, infrastructure, network, endpoint, backup, and security alerts, performing approved first-response actions and escalating issues that require additional expertise.
* Troubleshoot common hardware, software, operating system, Microsoft 365, identity, access, VPN, Wi-Fi, printing, and application issues while maintaining a professional customer-service experience.
* Perform approved service requests and operational tasks such as user onboarding, account and MFA support, device provisioning, software installation, patching, and equipment configuration.
* Perform initial security-event and phishing triage, following established procedures for investigation, containment, remediation, and escalation.
* Accurately document incidents, service requests, troubleshooting steps, resolutions, alert activity, and user communications in accordance with service-management requirements.
* Follow established SLAs, escalation procedures, security controls, change restrictions, and operational runbooks to ensure consistent and reliable service.
* Recognize issues that exceed Tier 1 authority or capability and provide complete, actionable escalations to Tier 2 or other specialized teams.
* Participate in shift handoffs and operational continuity by clearly communicating outstanding issues, service impacts, active alerts, and required follow-up.
* Contribute to knowledge articles, runbooks, and process improvements by identifying recurring issues, documenting solutions, and communicating opportunities for improved efficiency or service quality.
* Work collaboratively with users, Tier 2 technicians, vendors, and other IT teams to support timely resolution of incidents and service requests.

**Specialization Tracks**

**End User Support Focus**

* Primary emphasis on:
* Endpoint, desktop, mobile, and application support.
* Microsoft 365 and productivity applications.
* Software, hardware, printing, and remote support issues.
* Customer communication and service delivery.

Maintains working knowledge of: network monitoring, VPN, endpoint security, phishing/security triage, backup/infrastructure alerts, and NOC/SOC escalation.

**Network & Security Operations Focus**

Primary emphasis on:

* Infrastructure and network outage alert triage and outage resolution.
* User, endpoint, and systems security monitoring and triage.
* User connectivity, VPN, and access issue resolution.
* Veeam backup and SQL software job triage.

Maintains working knowledge of: Windows and endpoint troubleshooting, Microsoft 365, account/MFA support, hardware, applications, customer service, and service-desk procedures.

Requirements:

* Professional customer service and communication skills.
* Strong troubleshooting and analytical skills.
* Working knowledge of Windows and macOS.
* Microsoft 365 and common business applications.
* Basic understanding of networking, TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, Wi-Fi, and VPN concepts.
* Endpoint security and security monitoring fundamentals.
* Familiarity with cloud, backup, and infrastructure concepts.
* Basic identity and access management knowledge.
* Ability to accurately document work performed, troubleshooting and follow up steps within our ticketing system.
* Ability to follow technical procedures and assess when escalation is required.
* 0-1 year of IT support or customer service experience.
* Associate’s degree in computer science or equivalent work experience (preferred)

The Senior Manager, VEC Project Engagement serves as the critical connective tissue between Consumer Sales and Network Project Management teams. This role owns the translation layer between commercial priorities and network build/enablement execution, ensuring that sales commitments, market opportunities, and customer experience goals are matched to realistic, well-sequenced network capacity and infrastructure delivery.
  
  
This person is equally comfortable in a sales strategy conversation and a network engineering status review, and can move fluidly between the two, converting business urgency into engineering-ready requirements, and converting network constraints into sales-ready guidance.
  
  

* Serve as the primary liaison between VEC leadership and Network Project Management/Engineering teams, ensuring both sides operate from a shared view of priorities, timelines, and constraints.
* Translate sales demand into network requirements, working with network and sales leaders to understand market opportunity, promotional pushes, and customer commitments, then converting these into clear, prioritized asks for both teams.
* Own the project engagement lifecycle for VEC-related initiatives, from intake and scoping through execution tracking, risk escalation, and post-launch review, applying formal project/program management lifecycle discipline (SDLC/PMLC) to ensure consistent governance and delivery quality.
* Manage cross-functional governance, running regular joint forums (e.g., weekly/biweekly syncs, steering committees) between sales and network stakeholders to review pipeline, blockers, and enablement status.
* Build and maintain enablement roadmaps that align network build-out, capacity upgrades, and market readiness with sales go-to-market timing.
* Identify and resolve friction points where sales expectations outpace network readiness (or vice versa), proactively flagging risk and negotiating trade-offs with data-driven recommendations.
* Develop reporting and dashboards that give sales and network leadership visibility into project status, coverage/capacity readiness, and enablement milestones, leveraging AI-driven tools to automate data aggregation, surface insights faster, and reduce manual reporting effort.
* Own process improvement across the sales-to-network handoff, reducing rework, miscommunication, and delayed launches.
* Lead and support escalation management for high-priority markets, accounts, or launches where network enablement is on the critical path to sales targets.
* Partner with Finance/Strategy as needed to model the ROI and prioritization trade-offs of competing network investment requests driven by sales demand.

***This is a remote position with standard working hours from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) and up to 25% travel to support new market launches.***
**What We’re Looking For...**
**You’ll need to have:**

* Bachelor's degree or four or more years of work experience.
* Six or more years of relevant experience required, demonstrated through one or a combination of work and/or military experience, or specialized training.
* Six or more years of relevant work experience in partnership management, business development, channel sales, or a related field.
* Experience negotiating and managing third-party vendor or partner agreements.
* Experience leading teams or managing complex cross-functional initiatives.
* Experience in MDU, multifamily, property management, real estate, or proptech.
* Knowledge of the telecommunications, broadband, or connected-home landscape.
* Experience building a partner program or new sales channel from early stage to scale.
* Strong analytical skills, including building business cases and working with performance data to drive decisions.

**Even better if you have one or more of the following:**

* A degree in Business, Marketing, or a related field, or an MBA.
* Excellent executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders both inside and outside the company.
* Comfort working in ambiguity and moving quickly from idea to pilot to scaled program.

Position Summary
  
  
The Senior Program Manager, Network Build leads the delivery of fiber network construction across one or more markets and the Design Areas within them. This role owns the plan for each market from an accepted design package through an operational network, and is accountable for keeping every Design Area moving through the same sixteen milestones, from package accepted to operational. The Senior Program Manager sets the standard for how the Network Build Program Managers plan, report and escalate, and is the primary voice of the build program to senior leaders. The role also helps build and refine the processes the team runs on, so that planning, handoffs, reporting and vendor payment become more consistent and more efficient as the program grows.
  
  
Key Responsibilities
  
  
**Plan and schedule ownership**

* Own the schedule and plan logic for assigned markets, including dependencies, crew capacity, quantities, production rates and weather effects, and keep them accurate as work moves from Project Controls to the Network Build team.
* Maintain the sixteen-milestone plan for every Design Area, and decide when a milestone is complete using evidence from the responsible team rather than assumption.
* Re-forecast dates when crew counts, weather, permits or materials change, and explain the effect on the market finish date.

**Milestone management and handoffs**

* Confirm the Operational state of each Design Area. The Senior Program Manager and the Network Build Program Managers confirm it; no other team does.
* Manage the release of each project to construction, including the handoff to Supply Chain for materials staging and the notice to Sales and Marketing.
* In Prescott, run the pre-construction approval sequence: Construction completes the utility locates and reports to the Program Manager, the Program Manager schedules the pre-construction walks, Design and Engineering makes comments and corrections, the City approves, and Construction is then released.

**Cross-functional leadership**

* Coordinate Design and Engineering, the Permit Specialist, Supply Chain, Construction, Sales and Marketing and the Network Operations Center so that each handoff is clean and dated.
* Hold a weekly meeting with each team on Thursday or Friday, collect final updates by Monday, and prepare the reports for the Wednesday 30-60-90 day review.
* Escalate risks, delays and decisions early, with a recommendation and the effect on schedule and cost.

**Vendor and financial oversight**

* Make sure construction vendors are paid accurately and on time by reviewing each submitted invoice against the approved design prints before it is entered for payment.
* Track budget against forecast for each Design Area and flag variances to leadership.

**Reporting and governance**

* Report status using four labels: On Track, At-Risk, Off-Track and Complete.
* Track grant-funded markets against their commitments and prepare the reporting those programs require.
* Review the plan data for accuracy each week, and correct gaps before reports are issued.
* Communicate directly with executives and senior leaders in writing and in meetings, presenting status, risks, decisions and recommendations in plain language with the conclusion first.

**Team leadership**

* Coach and review the work of the Network Build Program Managers, set consistent reporting standards, and step in on the most complex or at-risk markets.

**Process development and improvement**

* Help design and document the processes the Network Build team follows, including milestone definitions, handoffs between teams, schedule updates, reporting and vendor invoice review.
* Review how the processes work in practice each quarter, identify recurring delays, rework and gaps, and recommend and lead improvements.
* Turn lessons from completed Design Areas into updated standards, templates and checklists that every Network Build Program Manager uses.
* Work with Design and Engineering, Permitting, Supply Chain, Construction, Sales and Marketing and the Network Operations Center to agree on process changes before they are adopted.
* Train and coach the Network Build Program Managers on new and revised processes, and confirm that they are followed.

**Qualifications**
**Required**

* A bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, business or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* At least eight years of program or project management experience, including at least five years delivering outside plant fiber, utility or telecommunications construction.
* Demonstrated ability to manage schedules with dependencies, crew capacity and weather, and to explain a forecast change in plain language.
* Experience managing construction vendors, including invoice review against design documents.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience preparing and presenting executive-level status reports, briefings and recommendations that are clear, accurate and concise.

**Preferred**

* Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent.
* Experience with federal or state broadband grant programs.
* Experience with permitting for rights-of-way, railroad, highway and utility pole attachments.
* Experience leading or mentoring other program managers.

What Success Looks Like
  
  

* Every Design Area in the assigned markets shows an accurate, current date for each milestone.
* Forecast dates move when crews, weather or permits change, and leaders hear about the change before the weekly review.
* Vendor invoices are verified against the design prints and paid without rework.
* Handoffs between teams happen on the planned date, with no team waiting for another.
* Processes are documented, current and followed, and improvements that came from completed Design Areas are visible in the team's standards and templates.

The Sr. Strategy and Programs Manager, FWA HSI Local Marketing Activation is the connection between FWA High Speed Internet local marketing strategy and what happens in market. This role owns how local marketing gets activated for FWA HSI: partnering with the HSI acquisition team to identify opportunities and priorities, deciding where, why, and how to activate, designing the programs that do it, and enabling the field to run those programs with confidence.
  
  
The role works where network capacity and demand are out of balance. That includes High Supply and Low Demand markets, where available capacity isn’t converting into activations, and markets where churn and disconnects are eroding growth. This person turns market-level data into targeted local programs, runs them, measures them, and scales what works.
  
  
This is not a project coordinator role. This person builds the activation programs, owns their delivery, and is accountable for whether they drive new accounts and retention in market.
  
  
This is a remote role. Travel expectation is up to 30% nationally, covering market visits, National Marketing engagements, planning sessions, and team collaboration. The best activation programs are designed by people who spend time in the markets they are building.
  
  
  
**Job Responsibilities**
**Activation Strategy & Program Design**

* Own the activation approach. Develop the framework for how FWA HSI local marketing gets activated: which markets, which audiences, which tactics, in what sequence, and what principles guide local decisions.
* Lead High Supply and Low Demand programs. Combine network capacity data with local marketing levers to build programs that convert available capacity into activation and define when a geography qualifies.
* Build complete program designs. Every program should have a clear objective, target audience, channel mix, offer and messaging direction, timeline, budget, and success metric, with rationale for each choice.
* Develop retention-oriented programs. Partner with the disconnect and churn effort to design local programs that reduce HSI churn, not just drive new orders.
* Close the gaps. Identify moments where the organization lacks a proven tactic or a defined approach for FWA HSI, and build the solution instead of flagging it for someone else.

**Program Execution & Field Enablement**

* Run the programs. Own program management from design through launch and close-out: timelines, dependencies, vendors, budgets, and cross-functional deliverables.
* Enable the field. Give the field everything it needs to execute: program briefs, targeting lists, messaging guidance, creative assets, and clear success criteria.
* Sequence the rollout. Pilot first, then scale in phases, tied to the commercial calendar and to the team’s 2027 expansion into HSI.
* Make it stick. Partner with the Hyperlocal Playbook Manager so proven programs are captured in the playbook as operating standards.

**Measurement & Test-and-Learn**

* Design the tests. Build test-and-control structures for local programs so the team can separate real lift from noise.
* Target with data. Use propensity and segmentation analysis to choose and size markets and opportunity.
* Report what works. Produce clear readouts on incremental new accounts, churn impact, cost per acquisition, and program ROI, and recommend scale, adjust, or stop.
* Close the loop. Run a retrospective at the end of each program and each quarter: what the program produced, where execution diverged from the plan, and what changes next.

**Cross-Functional Partnership**

* Partner with National Marketing. Pull national campaigns, brand guardrails, and creative into field-ready formats, and push field learnings back up so what gets built centrally serves local needs.
* Partner with HSI Acquisition team to identify commercial opportunities and priorities for hyperlocal marketing campaigns
* Partner with Network and Capacity Planning. Get timely, usable capacity data so programs target the right markets at the right time.
* Partner with Analytics and Sales Operations. Align on data, measurement, and incentives so programs are measurable and the frontline is incented to action off of them.
* Coordinate with the Fiber team. Manage the places where FWA and fiber overlap, including footprint eligibility changes and creating an ecosystem accounting for customer moves from HSI to fiber.
* Steward the brand. Ensure local activity stays within T-Mobile brand guardrails while remaining locally effective.

**Quarterly Planning & Field Intelligence**

* Contribute to the planning cycle. Translate commercial targets, capacity conditions, and national priorities into a 90-day activation program plan with market-by-market priorities.
* Synthesize the signal. Aggregate market observations, competitive activity, and program performance into insights that inform local decisions and national direction.
* Find the pattern. Identify which market conditions, audiences, and tactic combinations are producing results and what the team should do more of.
* Brief leadership. Produce a regular update for the Sr. Manager and Director on what’s working, what isn’t, and what the field needs.

* Bachelor's Degree and 7 years of related work experience, or a combination of education and experience deemed equivalent
* 7-10 years in marketing strategy, field marketing, growth marketing, or program management, with demonstrated ownership of programs from design through measurement.
* Strong analytical skills, including campaign measurement, segmentation, and test-and-control design.
* Experience managing complex, cross-functional programs with many stakeholders and no direct authority.

**About Cape**
Cape is America’s privacy-first mobile carrier. Our mission is to be a force for good in global wireless. Cape was founded in 2022 by people who believe privacy is a fundamental right, not a luxury to be traded away. Our journey began when our founder recognized a critical vulnerability in our modern world: everyone relies on the same stagnant cellular infrastructure and legacy systems that track our every movement, monitor and profile our connections, and lose and sell our personal data.
  
  
Instead of accepting the status quo, we decided to fix it. National security professionals, journalists, parents, and everyone in between can stay connected
*and*
have privacy.
  
  
We didn’t just build a layer on top of old tech; we built America’s most private and secure mobile carrier from the ground up. By building our own network from scratch, we are able to design and build a suite of privacy and security features that no other carrier on the planet can offer.
  
  
Today, Cape provides our secure network to consumers, businesses, and government agencies alike. We closed our Series C in March 2026, and we are scaling rapidly, with the goal of giving people back control of their most personal information.
  
  
**The Team**
At Cape, we are the architects of a privacy-centric movement that is just getting started. We are relentless builders, constantly innovating at the edge of what's possible in telecommunications. We operate on a foundation of high trust and high expectations. Our structure is flat, and collaboration matters more than hierarchy. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with world-class engineers, architects, and visionaries, and work across organizational lines to solve "impossible" problems and deliver mission-critical results for our users every single day.
  
  
**The Role:**
Cape's network team designs how traffic actually moves through our infrastructure: routing, regional connectivity, subscriber provisioning, and the vendor-implemented changes that make it all work. Right now, that work is coordinated ad hoc, and the team needs someone to take real ownership of task tracking, timeline accountability, and communication across engineering, business development, and vendors. This role is the first of its kind in the network team. We're looking for a Program Manager who is technical enough to challenge engineering estimates, sanity-check what BD is promising customers, and set delivery timelines the team can actually hit.
  
  
You'll work in close partnership with the network operations lead to roadmap upcoming work, surface dependencies and conflicts before they become fire drills, and keep vendors accountable to what they've committed to. Telco or network experience is a plus, but we care more about startup instincts and a bias toward realistic, forward-moving plans than about a background in telecom specifically.
  
  
**What You'll Work On:**

* Own Jira hygiene and task tracking for the network team, bringing structure to work that is currently coordinated informally
* Build a reliable system for tracking work, exposing dependencies, and catching timeline slips early, across network engineering, BD, and vendors
* Partner closely with the network team's technical lead to roadmap infrastructure work like routing, regional connectivity, subscriber provisioning, and cloud/vendor integrations
* Pressure-test proposed timelines and BD requests for technical feasibility before commitments are made externally
* Host vendor meetings and hold vendors accountable to their delivery commitments
* Deconflict priorities and dependencies across the network team and adjacent teams, including consumer-facing projects
* Translate technical network work for non-technical stakeholders, and translate business requests back into realistic technical asks for engineering
* Help define the org model for how program management, technical ownership, and execution responsibilities fit together on the network team as it scales

**Experience:**

* Technical program management experience in a fast-moving engineering environment, ideally at a startup
* A track record of bringing structure to ambiguous, cross-team work without slowing it down
* Comfort learning a new technical domain quickly and deeply enough to challenge engineering judgment and assess feasibility, not just track progress
* Experience building systems for tracking work, surfacing dependencies, and holding owners accountable to deadlines
* Strong communication skills; able to translate between technical teams and business/vendor stakeholders
* Comfort engaging directly with external vendors and holding them to their commitments
* (Bonus) Experience with network or telco infrastructure: traffic routing, cloud connectivity, configuration, or subscriber provisioning
* (Bonus) Experience at a company building or operating physical/network infrastructure rather than pure software
* (Bonus) Prior experience supporting consumer products alongside more technical/infrastructure work

**About Us**

Medical data exchange is one of the biggest unsolved problems in US healthcare. If you've spent any real time in the healthcare system, you've felt it, and it only gets worse the sicker and older you get. Metriport exists to fix that. We connect to the data sources the healthcare providers of tomorrow need, take raw data that's unusable in its source form, and turn it into a single clean format that care teams, and their agents, actually use to improve outcomes. Record retrieval across thousands of legacy systems and antiquated data pipes that used to take weeks now takes seconds. Clinicians walk into appointments with the full patient picture already in hand, and that speed can mean spotting a condition early enough to actually treat it.

We're not a healthcare company. We're a technology company that happens to operate in healthcare, and we build every layer ourselves: acquisition, transform, and insight. Legacy EHRs were built to get providers paid, not to serve the clinical experience. We're building what should have existed instead: the system of record for all of US healthcare. We started in data exchange. Today we compete with the largest data platforms in the space. Tomorrow we will be the infrastructure layer healthcare runs on.

We've found product-market fit (multi-million dollar ARR, 100+ customers including Amazon One Medical, Circle Medical, Color Health, and Strive Health) and we're backed by top-tier VCs with years of runway ahead of us. **Position Summary**

  

At Frontlion, the Customer Success Manager is the business owner for a portfolio of accounts. You are not a help desk and you are not a passive relationship manager. You are the customer’s trusted advisor and our commercial lead on the account. You run the adoption plan, the business reviews, the renewal, and the expansion conversation. You see the whole picture: usage, health, outcomes, and dollars, and you move the account forward on purpose. You report directly to the VP of Customer Experience & Operations.

  
  

**What You Own**

  

Your portfolio has a scorecard. These are the numbers you are measured on and the numbers you are expected to move.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  

**NRR**

  

Net Revenue Retention across your book. Grow the base through expansion and strong renewals.

  

**GRR**

  

Gross Revenue Retention. Protect the dollars and logos you start the year with
**.**

New ARR from upsell and expansion inside your existing accounts.

  
  
  

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

  
  

Run your portfolio like a business owner

  

  
* Build and maintain an account plan for every customer: their goals, their health, their renewal date, their expansion path, and your next move to win the day, the week, the month, and the contract.
  
* Know your numbers cold: ARR, renewal timing, adoption, and risk, and bring a point of view on where each account is headed.
  
* Prioritize your time against revenue and risk, not against whoever emailed last.
  

  
  

Drive adoption and real outcomes.

  

  
* Lead onboarding and ongoing enablement so customers get to value fast and keep getting more of it.
  
* Run business reviews on a deliberate cadence that ties usage and results back to the outcomes the customer cares about.
  
* Maintain deep command of the Frontlion platform and roadmap so customers are always using it to its fullest.
  

  
  

Grow the account: upsell and expansion.

  

  
* Actively hunt for expansion inside your book: new sites, new departments, added products, higher tiers, and usage growth.
  
* Build the business case, price it, and lead the expansion conversation to close. This is a commercial role, and growing your portfolio is the job, not a bonus.
  
* Partner with Sales and leadership on larger expansions, but own the motion inside your accounts end to end.
  

  
  

Protect the base: retention and renewals.

  

  
* Own renewals in your portfolio from start to finish: forecast them early, reduce their risk, negotiate terms, and close them on time.
  
* Spot churn and contraction risk before it shows up in the numbers, and run the save play with the right internal resources.
  
* Defend GRR. Treat every renewal as yours to win and every dollar at risk as yours to keep.
  

  
  

Be the voice of the customer inside Frontlion.

  

  
* Lead escalations: pull in Support, Product, and Engineering and drive issues to resolution on the customer’s timeline.
  
* Feed clear, prioritized customer signal back into Product and leadership.
  
* Report regularly to the VP of Customer Experience & Operations on account health, retention, risk, and expansion pipeline.

* Commercial instinct: comfortable talking price, terms, ROI, and business cases with decision makers.
  
* Strong business and data sense. You can read an account’s numbers and turn them into a plan.
  
* Confident, credible communicator with executives and operators alike.

Your performance is read off your portfolio, not off activity:

At Frontlion, the Customer Success Manager is the business owner for a portfolio of accounts. You are not a help desk and you are not a passive relationship manager. **What You Own**

*Your portfolio has a scorecard. These are the numbers you are measured on and the numbers you are expected to move.*

**NRR**

Net Revenue Retention across your book. Grow the base through expansion and strong renewals.

**GRR**

Gross Revenue Retention. Protect the dollars and logos you start the year with**.**

**Expansion**

New ARR from upsell and expansion inside your existing accounts.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

*Run your portfolio like a business owner*

* Build and maintain an account plan for every customer: their goals, their health, their renewal date, their expansion path, and your next move to win the day, the week, the month, and the contract.

* Prioritize your time against revenue and risk, not against whoever emailed last.

* Run business reviews on a deliberate cadence that ties usage and results back to the outcomes the customer cares about.
* Maintain deep command of the Frontlion platform and roadmap so customers are always using it to its fullest.

*Grow the account: upsell and expansion.*

* Actively hunt for expansion inside your book: new sites, new departments, added products, higher tiers, and usage growth.
* Build the business case, price it, and lead the expansion conversation to close. This is a commercial role, and growing your portfolio is the job, not a bonus.
* Partner with Sales and leadership on larger expansions, but own the motion inside your accounts end to end.

*Protect the base: retention and renewals.*

* Own renewals in your portfolio from start to finish: forecast them early, reduce their risk, negotiate terms, and close them on time.
* Spot churn and contraction risk before it shows up in the numbers, and run the save play with the right internal resources.
* Defend GRR. Treat every renewal as yours to win and every dollar at risk as yours to keep.

*Be the voice of the customer inside Frontlion.*

* Lead escalations: pull in Support, Product, and Engineering and drive issues to resolution on the customer’s timeline.
* Feed clear, prioritized customer signal back into Product and leadership.
* Report regularly to the VP of Customer Experience & Operations on account health, retention, risk, and expansion pipeline.
